title: Design a test that detects a real bug
scope: Reason about a selected mutant; no submitted-test execution

items.prompt: A projection function incorrectly returns the zero vector for every input. Which test rejects it? A: project [0,1] onto [1,0]. B: project [1,0] onto [1,0]. Return A or B.
items.solution: A has a correct zero projection; B must return a nonzero vector.
hints: Identify the requested quantity and its units before calculating.
Write the equation using the supplied inputs, then check units and signs.
A has a correct zero projection; B must return a nonzero vector.
items.remediation: Compare one intermediate result with the stated model. Revisit /lessons/PY07 or try the other scenario. This is a suggestion, not a diagnosis.

items.prompt: An FK implementation returns the correct x,y but hardcodes orientation to zero. Which discriminating test should you add? A: q1=0,q2=0. B: q1=π/2,q2=0. Validate every returned pose field. Return A or B. Tolerance ±0.001 for numeric fields; follow the stated units.
items.solution: Choice B distinguishes the mutated behavior from a valid implementation. Explain both expected outcomes before writing the test locally; submitted tests are not executed.
